speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly what these unusual physical features look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Salt-Wasting or Simple Virilizing type), likely due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

I have noted your history of virilization (clitoromegaly, labial fusion) at birth, severe acne, bone fractures, and delayed menarche. Before I confirm this, please confirm if you have experienced excessive hair growth on your body or if you have ever been told you have high blood pressure or low potassium levels.
